Hadhrat Huwaytib bin Abdil Uzza (RA) Accepts Islaam
Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) invites Hadhrat Huwaytib bin Abdil Uzza (RA) to Islaam and he Accepts

Hadhrat Mundhir bin Jahm (RA) narrates from Hadhrat Huwaytib bin Abdil Uzza (RA) that he was terrified when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Makkah when it was conquered. He left his house and scattered his family in various places where they would be safe. He then hid himself in an orchard belonging to the Auf clan. He narrates, "One day, Abu Dharr suddenly arrived. We had been good friends before and friendship always bears fruit. However, as soon as I saw him, I started to run away." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) called out, "O Abu Muhammad!" When Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA) responded, Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) asked, "What is the matter?" "Fear," replied, Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA). "Have no fear," said Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), "You have amnesty in the protection of Allaah." Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA) then went back and greeted Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA).
"You may go home," said Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA). "How am I to go home?" asked Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA), "By Allaah! I do not see myself returning home alive. I shall be met on the street and killed or be killed by someone barging into my house. In addition, my family are scattered in various places." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "Then gather your family in one place and I shall escort you home." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) then took Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA) home and announced, "Huwaytib has been granted amnesty and may not be harmed." When Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and informed him about the events, he said, "Has everyone not been granted amnesty besides those whose execution I have ordered?" This statement put Hadhrat Huwaytib t's heart at ease and he took his family home.
Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) again came to Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA) and said, "O Abu Muhammad! Until when? Where to? You have participated in all the battles. Although you have lost tremendous good, much good is still left for you. Go to Rasulullaah ﷺ and accept Islaam. You will then be able to live in peace. Rasulullaah ﷺ is the most righteous of people, the one who best maintains family ties and the most tolerant of all people. His honour is yours and his dignity is yours." Hadhrat Huwaytib (RA) then said to Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), "I am prepared to accompany you to Rasulullaah ﷺ."
